item.title: Inside the Numbers: Texas found a recipe for success
item.description: AUSTIN, TX - NOVEMBER 21: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning #16 runs with the ball as Arkansas Razorbacks defensive back Shelton Lewis #2 pursues during the SEC football game between Texas Longhorns and Arkansas Razorbacks on November 21, 2026, at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The No. 5 Texas Longhorns looked like flat track bully for the second time in three weeks, dominating the Arkansas Razorbacks in the home finale on Saturday at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Arch Manning was dealing, the offense was humming, and the defense was once again dominant, imposing their will on Arkansas from wire to wire. Now, the Longhorns are playing for style points, trying to secure their place in the postseason hierarchy. Arch Manning: 21-25, 287 yards, 2 TD Following Arch Manning is enough to give you whiplash. After having the worst games of his career, he turned in one of the best — thanks in large part to the game plan. After going away from the short game against LSU, much to the detriment of the offense, the Longhorns leaned back into it against Arkansas and feasted. Manning was a perfect 10-of-10 on passing attempts at or behind the line of scrimmage, averaging 10.7 yards per attempt at that range . If you add in anything shorter than five yards, 141 (49 percent) of his passing yardage in the game came in the short game. At one point, Manning completed nine consecutive passes, the longest streak of the season, six of them going for either a first down or a touchdown. That streak includes four of the Texas explosive passing plays on it, including Emmett Mosley V’s 17-yard touchdown to end the first half. That was one of Mosley’s eight receptions for 106 yards on the day, his first 100-yard game as a Longhorn. Third downs: 6-11 (54.5 percent) The Texas offense has been rightfully criticized for its third-down performance this year, sitting near the bottom of the conference in third-down conversions, but they bucked that trend on Saturday. Converting six of 11 gives them their best conversion percentage since the start of conference play, averaging an abysmal 34.6 percent since they started SEC games in September. A big part of their success was how they set themselves up for third and short, which is obviously the optimal outcome for an offense. They averaged 5.3 yards on an average distance of 4.9 yards, needing to gain four or fewer yards on six of their 11 attempts. First-down success set Texas up for manageable third downs or avoided them entirely, averaging 9.1 yards per play, including 12.6 yards per attempt for Arch Manning. Texas scored three first-down touchdowns — a 21-yard pass to tight end Emaree Winston, a one-yard rush by Michael Terry set up by a 30-yard first-down pass to Raleek Brown, and a fourth-quarter exclamation point by Derrek Cooper. (Photo by Rebecca Villagracia/Getty Images) Louisville and Lincoln Kienholz picked up an emphatic victory on Saturday over Pittsburgh. Kienholz threw five touchdowns, and the Cardinals won 42-10. It was a fun day to be Louisville. That is, until the postgame press conference when Kienholz was asked about his future. In modern college football, players — especially quarterbacks — get asked about what they’re doing next as if they’re a free agent. They sort of are. Kienholz had just arrived at Louisville this season after transferring from Ohio State, so he’s not a stranger to the transfer portal. With one week remaining in the regular season, Kienholz was asked the tough question on Saturday. The way he handled it has some Louisville fans worried. It’s more of just those guys just focused on those things so I can focus on football.” On the one hand, that’s a fair answer. Kienholz doesn’t owe anyone a deeper explanation than that right now. On the other hand, it does sound like a guy who isn’t exactly committing himself to Louisville’s 2027 roster. It’d be tough for Louisville to lose Kienholz, but if he chooses to leave, he’d have plenty of interested teams chasing after him in the portal. item.title: Chiefs Make Rare Patrick Mahomes Decision Days Before Bills Game
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 22: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs reacts against the Arizona Cardinals during the third quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs’ blowout against the Arizona Cardinals was so lopsided that CBS switched to another game. With the Chiefs facing the Buffalo Bills in a matter of days, head coach Andy Reid opted to take some precaution with Patrick Mahomes. With the Chiefs leading the Cardinals 34-7 in the fourth quarter, Reid decided to rest Mahomes and inserted Justin Fields as the team’s quarterback to close out the game. It is worth noting that Mahomes is just two weeks removed from sustaining what looked to be a scary elbow injury. Mahomes has been able to play through the injury without missing time. With the game out of reach, Reid opted not to risk Mahomes sustaining further injury. Here’s what you need to know about the latest Chiefs news. The Chiefs Turned to Justin Fields as Patrick Mahomes Continues to Recover From Elbow Injury Kansas City traded for Fields during the offseason as insurance behind Mahomes as the quarterback was recovering from a season-ending ACL injury at the time of the deal. Reid has been outspoken about his trust in Fields. “I like his game,” Reid said regarding Fields during a March media session, per Pro Football Talk. “He can do the drop back game, he can do the movement stuff, play-action — whether it’s a naked or a sprint-out game. “He has that whole package that he can do. He understands the screen game, understands how to set it up. He obviously — he’s going to be one of the better athletes on the field when he’s out there,” Reid continued. “He’s fast, big, likes to play the game. So, I mean, all the stuff I like.” Chiefs vs. Bills: Kansas City Is a 3-Point Underdog Against Buffalo in NFL Odds for Thanksgiving Game The Chiefs will travel to Buffalo for a holiday matchup against the Bills. item.title: JJ Spaun Makes History With Stunning Eight-Shot Victory at Dunlop Phoenix
item.description: Jun 15, 2025; Oakmont, Pennsylvania, USA; JJ Spaun celebrates with the championship trophy after winning the 125th U.S. Open golf tournament. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Orlando Fuller JJ Spaun has claimed his third victory of the year after winning the Dunlop Phoenix Tournament in Japan by eight shots. The 36-year-old American finished at 16-under 264 at Phoenix Country Club in Miyazaki, with Yusaku Hosono finishing second. Spaun had not played since winning the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth on September 20 . He returned to competition after more than two months away and produced another impressive performance to win his second consecutive event. The 2025 U.S. Open champion opened with a six-under 66 before carding a 70 in the second round. However, his performance over the weekend put him well clear of the rest of the field and secured the biggest winning margin of his season. Spaun Takes Control With 62 in Third Round Spaun made his move in the third round, shooting an eight-under 62 on the par-70 course. His round included seven birdies and an eagle, giving him a commanding lead heading into Sunday’s final round. He then followed it with another strong performance, making five birdies to shoot a four-under 66. That took him to 16 under for the tournament and gave him an eight-shot advantage over Hosono. The victory came at an event that has welcomed several major names in golf over the years. Johnny Miller, Seve Ballesteros, Tom Watson, Ernie Els and David Duval have all won the Dunlop Phoenix. Tiger Woods also claimed the title in 2004 and 2005, while Brooks Koepka won consecutive editions in 2016 and 2017. Spaun has now added his name to that list after dominating the tournament across the final two rounds. Spaun Adds Dunlop Phoenix Title to Successful 2026 Season Spaun’s latest victory follows his win at the BMW PGA Championship, where he finished two shots clear of Rory McIlroy, Adam Scott and Aaron Rai. He produced a final-round 67 at Wentworth to claim the title after missing out on a place in the U.S. Presidents Cup team. The American had been disappointed with his omission from Brandt Snedeker’s team for the competition at Medinah. He had expected to be part of the team before the captain selected Jacob Bridgeman and Jackson Koivun as his final two picks. Spaun instead travelled to Wentworth and won the tournament in his first appearance at the DP World Tour event. He has now followed that result with another title after returning from his two-month break. His other victory this year came at the PGA Tour’s Valero Texas Open in April, the week before the Masters. The Dunlop Phoenix win gives him three titles in 2026 and continues a strong run for the world No. 13. Other notable players in Japan included Ryo Ishikawa, who finished tied for fourth, while former LIV Golf player and NCAA champion Michael La Sasso finished tied for 11th. item.title: ‘That offense is pathetic’: Urban Meyer says Michigan offense ‘stinks’ ahead of Ohio State showdown
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Ohio State Buckeyes and Michigan Wolverines are both limping into this year’s edition of The Game, with each program closing out a disappointing regular season and each head coach facing questions about his future. Ohio State’s College Football Playoff hopes ended with a loss at Nebraska on Saturday, and while Michigan pulled off a stunning upset of No. 4 UCLA later that night, the win only got the Wolverines to 6-5. Now, former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer has offered his prediction for next Saturday’s matchup in Columbus. And while Meyer had plenty of praise for Michigan’s defense, he called the Wolverines’ offense “pathetic” and said he expects a low-scoring game. Disappointing Seasons For Both Ohio State’s season has fallen apart over the last month. The Buckeyes started 6-1, but quarterback Julian Sayin suffered an arm injury late in a 19-15 win over Indiana, and they’ve since lost to USC, Oregon, and now Nebraska with freshman Luke Fahey under center. Saturday’s 31-28 loss in Lincoln dropped Ohio State to 7-4 and officially knocked the Buckeyes out of playoff contention. Needless to say, the criticism of Ryan Day has never been louder. Michigan’s season hasn’t gone any better under first-year head coach Kyle Whittingham. The Wolverines have flip-flopped between Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr at quarterback, and they entered Saturday ranked 131st in the country in scoring at 18.3 points per game. But Michigan’s defense kept the Wolverines in it against UCLA, and they won 18-16 in triple overtime when Underwood threw a 2-point conversion pass to Jalen Hoffman. The win handed the Bruins their first loss of the season and made Michigan bowl-eligible. Still, one upset isn’t likely to change much for Whittingham, whose future at Michigan is expected to be decided after the season. Neither team is exactly making a strong case for this year’s game, either. Before Michigan’s win, Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy, who is a longtime Michigan fan, called it the “worst big game” in the history of the rivalry and said both programs need an embarrassing loss so they can fire their coaches. ‘Their offense stinks’ Speaking on stage at a recent event, Meyer said Michigan’s defense deserves a lot of credit for how the Wolverines have stayed competitive this season, in a clip shared by Eleven Warriors . “I think the Wolverine defense is legit, legit, because that offense is pathetic up there. It’s the worst offense in college football, yet they’re in almost all the games. And we covered them on Big Noon a bunch. And their defense, what they did to UCLA, was absolutely phenomenal,” Meyer said. He then turned to his former team, noting that the Buckeyes haven’t been consistent on either side of the ball. “Our defense has been up and down a little bit, but their offense stinks. Our offense has been up and down a little bit, and now we’re down to our backup quarterback. So I see this being a very low-scoring game.

MIAMI – As Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo headlined the injury report ahead of Sunday night’s game against the Oklahoma City Thunder, he wasn’t the only top star to be featured. item.description: Kerby Joseph waited 406 days to return to the football field, and apparently, he was hoping Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield would give him a welcome-back present. Unfortunately for Joseph, Mayfield wasn’t interested in cooperating. Following the Detroit Lions’ 31-21 victory over Tampa Bay on Sunday afternoon at Ford Field, Joseph had some fun with reporters when asked whether his long-awaited return went better than expected. “Nah, man, I need a pick, man. I need a pick,” Joseph said, according to Kory Woods of MLive. “It’s all right. I ain’t get it. They don’t want to throw the ball down there. They scared. Baker, it’s all right. Honestly, I’m just happy we got the dub. It’s not all about me, man. It’s about the team. So we get this dub, man, I’m fine. I still want that pick, but they got to throw it deep.” Well, welcome back, Kerby! Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Kerby Joseph Brings Confidence Back to Lions Secondary Joseph was making his first appearance since October 2025 after battling a lingering knee injury that kept him sidelined for more than a year. Despite serious questions surrounding his recovery , the All-Pro safety finally returned to action Sunday. According to the MLive report, Joseph played 46 defensive snaps and recorded two solo tackles. He didn’t come away with the interception he wanted, but his return provided a welcome boost for a Detroit defense dealing with several significant injuries. item.title: Great escape? ESPN loses 7 million pay-TV homes following UFC departure
item.description: BRISTOL, CONNECTICUT - NOVEMBER 03: A logo sign at the entrance to the ESPN headquarters on November 03, 2024 in Bristol, Connecticut. (Photo by Kirby Lee/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN’s traditional television footprint continues to shrink — and Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) may have picked an ideal time to find a new broadcast partner . ESPN and ESPN2 are each available in approximately 54 million pay-TV homes, according to Disney’s latest annual filing . That represents a loss of seven million subscribers from Sept. 2025, when both networks reportedly reached roughly 61 million homes. At its peak in 2011, ESPN was available in approximately 100 million households. At ESPN’s reported $9.42 monthly carriage fee, New York Post estimates the seven-million-home decline represents more than $791 million in annualized carriage-fee value. However, that figure does not account for rate increases or ESPN’s growing direct-to-consumer business. Those shrinking subscriber totals have not stopped ESPN from opening its wallet for its biggest personalities. Stephen A. Smith signed a five-year contract reportedly worth approximately $100 million in 2025 — roughly $20 million annually. ESPN also agreed to pay approximately $85 million over five years to license The Pat McAfee Show , averaging $17 million per year. That McAfee figure covers the entire program and its production costs, not simply his salary. Together, the deals represent approximately $185 million in reported commitments while ESPN and ESPN2 have lost 12 million pay-TV homes since 2024, falling from 66 million to 54 million. Who doesn’t love Smith and McAfee, right? Can you feel my sarcasm? The timing is certainly interesting for fight fans. After seven years with ESPN, UFC moved its entire United States schedule to Paramount+ at the beginning of 2026. Paramount paid $7.7 billion for the seven-year agreement , averaging $1.1 billion annually — more than double the reported value of UFC’s previous ESPN deal. The move also eliminated UFC’s expensive pay-per-view model . Every numbered event and “Fight Night” card is now included with a Paramount+ subscription, while select major events are simulcast on CBS. To be clear, UFC’s departure did not cause ESPN to lose seven million pay-TV homes. The figures also measure ESPN and ESPN2 distribution, not subscriptions to ESPN’s standalone streaming service. Nevertheless, the decline illustrates the rapidly changing sports-media business UFC left behind. ESPN still controls a massive collection of valuable sports rights — and recently landed WWE premium live events — but its traditional cable reach is now nearly half what it was 15 years ago. Did UFC get out at exactly the right time ?

The Ferrari team principal spoke to reporters after the race on Nov. 21, in which Leclerc dived up the inside of Hamilton at Turn 7 on lap 38, while Hamilton was running sixth and chasing the two McLarens. The contact sent Hamilton across the run-off, and the stewards found Leclerc wholly to blame and gave him a 10-second time penalty. Leclerc crossed the line sixth but was classified 10th, and Hamilton finished seventh. It happened even though the team had passed a message to Leclerc during the race. Before the contact, the two had traded complaints on the radio about each other’s driving. The field was bunched up, and they were together on track for much of the race, fighting the McLaren pair, Alpine and Arvid Lindblad. Hamilton gave his side after the race . item.title: 7 Winners and 2 Losers from the Chiefs’ win over the Cardinals
item.description: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Your Kansas City Chiefs made it look easy on Sunday, burying the Arizona Cardinals 34-7. They needed this one with the Thanksgiving matchup with Buffalo looming large over the next four days. The home team played as clean a game as I can recall, committing no turnovers, allowing only one sack and being called for just two penalties. This one was never in doubt and was exactly the kind of game we wanted to see on a short week. Here are a few who stood out on Sunday as the Chiefs stayed hot. 7 Winners Running back Emmett Johnson: The silver lining of Ken Walker’s injury is the opportunity it has afforded Emmett Johnson— the kid has been incredible. In three quarters of snaps, Emmett Johnson racked up another 143 yards and a touchdown. He should seriously be in the OROY conversation— and lots of conversations in the Chiefs’ offensive meetings over the next few months as they figure out how to employ Ken and Emmitt together down the stretch. Tight end Travis Kelce: Kelce’s first target of the day fell incomplete. But he made up for it with the next six catches, including two touchdowns. Another week, another throwback performance for the GOAT. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes: When it clicks, it’s a thing of beauty. Mahomes continues to perform at an MVP level (another 300+ yards and 3 TDs) without having to play “hero ball.” He’s executing at a high level in the pocket, and burying teams early. Patrick Mahomes with a great running game and competent receivers is literally unstoppable. Defensive end George Karlaftis : Mahomes and Johnson will get the headlines, but Karlaftis was a spectacular counterpart on the defensive side of the ball. On Sunday, Furious George added five more QB hits, 2.5 sacks, and 2 tackles for loss to his season totals. Cornerback Nohl Williams : Two passes defended, a QB hit, and two of the biggest tackles of the game— one ended a drive with a stop right at the sticks on 4th down; the other hit was a WWE-style body slam. Nohl Williams is more than on pace for Pro Bowl/All Pro recognition in his second season. Wide receiver Xavier Worthy: He wasn’t able to haul in that deep pass, but he did catch a short pass on a sprint out of the backfield and take it in for a score. Expectations for Worthy should be reset— Josh Downs and Rashee Rice should get more of the volume, but Xavier can be the new Mecole Hardman, which is a very useful player in the Chiefs’ offense. Kicker Harrison Butker: Give credit where it’s due. Harrison Butker came through on Sunday, hitting all four extra points and two extra points. item.title: Bills report card: Buffalo's offense is starting to look second rate
item.description: ORCHARD PARK - The Buffalo Bills accomplished coach Joe Brady’s weekly mandate as they went 1-0 Sunday afternoon with their 26-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins . “I enjoy winning. I enjoy it for the guys, but we’ve got to continue to get better,” Brady said, no smile in sight because he knew his 9-1 team played down to the level of the competition against the 1-9 Dolphins, especially the offense, which despite some good-looking box score numbers was from efficient or sharp. “I know as the head football coach I always have to find ways for us to improve and get us to where we want to get to,” Brady said. “There’s a lot for us to clean up, and we’ve got to do it in a short time because we’ve got a short turnaround. As you guys have slowly learned of me, I’m never happy after games.” Yeah, but this time he actually had plenty of reasons to be unhappy. The Bills won by 17 points, they piled up 25 first downs and 405 yards of offense, but anyone who watched this game knows it was not pretty most of the way. All you need to know is that against a banged up Miami defense, the Bills managed only two touchdowns while settling for four Tyler Bass field goals. “They get paid on that side, too,” said Josh Allen, leaning on one of his stock quotes after games. “They made some plays tonight, they got some really young talent over there. I thought we communicated well, just a couple things here or there that can really help us become the offense that we want to be. And we're looking forward to do that.” Many fans don’t care because yes, the Bills went 1-0. And you can do that when you’re playing an overmatched backup QB for the fourth week in a row, but 1-0 will likely be 0-1 Thursday night if the Bills don’t play better when Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs come to town. “We know what type of team they are,” Allen said of the 8-2 Chiefs who breezed to a 34-7 victory over the hapless Cardinals Sunday. “They've been one of the best teams in the league the last 10 years. So you got to play your best, and tonight I don't feel like I did. Got a lot to clean up, just trying to move forward.” Here’s how I graded the Bills: PASS OFFENSE: C Josh Allen’s final numbers would lead you to believe he had another of those Allen days that we’ve all come to expect against Miami. Don’t be fooled, it wasn’t, and he was the first to admit that after the game. Yes, he piled up 304 passing yards, but his overall performance was sub par as he continually made puzzling decisions with the ball, threw two interceptions (plus had another wiped out by a penalty), missed some easy button short throws, and took three sacks for 24 yards in losses. He didn’t get much help from his offensive line which had a disappointing day against an undermanned Miami front as he faced more pressure than anyone could have expected. item.title: Aaron Rodgers makes clear what he doesn’t want to do after Pittsburgh Steelers loss
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers was frustrated after the team’s 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. The Philadelphia ended a seven-game losing streak with a surprise win against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Steelers failed to score a touchdown in the first three quarters, and Max Hurleman’s score in the fourth came too late. Speaking after the game, Aaron Rodgers told the Steelers’ press conference that the offense was too one-dimensional – and he did not want to be throwing the ball so much. Rodgers said: “Run the ball. Yeah, we like to run the ball. That makes everything easier. “We’re not trying to throw the ball 50 times a game.” Rodgers added that obviously circumstances can influence the game plan – but he believes the Steelers’ offense relies on a strong running game. “Some games might dictate some of that stuff, but we got to run the football and generate explosive runs, and that sets up everything else.” Rodgers praises Eagles Veteran quarterback Rodgers praised the Philadelphia Eagles defense, and admitted this was the reason why he had to throw the ball so much. Rodgers said: “We weren’t running very well. They got a good defense. “They haven’t won a lot of games, but the defense was playing pretty good for the most part. They got high draft picks and good players and guys that gotten paid, and we knew it was going to be a challenge, but we had plenty of opportunities. “We got to win games,” he added, referring to the Steelers’ fading playoff chances. The loss leaves the Steelers at 6-4, the same record as the Cleveland Browns. The Cincinnati Bengals lead the division at 7-2. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
